$comment: Visual selection mapping for spec-driven reports. Rules are grounded in Microsoft guidance: 'Tips for designing a great Power BI dashboard' (service-dashboards-design-tips), 'Visualizations overview in Power BI' (power-bi-visualizations-overview) and 'Design Power BI reports for accessibility' (desktop-accessibility). Test-ReportLayout reads this file, so editing it changes the lint.

intents.need: State one number that is the headline of the page.
intents.question: What is the total / the rate right now?
intents.because: A card shows one number prominently. Use it only when there is no target and no time axis to compare against.
intents.avoid_when: A goal exists (use kpi) or the value only means something as a trend (use line).

intents.need: Show progress and distance to a target.
intents.question: Are we on plan?
intents.because: KPI shows the latest value, the trend and the distance to the goal in one visual.
intents.avoid_when: There is no target measure: the KPI degrades to a plain number, so use a card.

intents.need: Show current status inside a fixed range with a target.
intents.question: Where are we between the floor and the ceiling?
intents.because: Microsoft: gauge charts are great for displaying the current status in the context of a goal. Circular charts are otherwise discouraged.
intents.avoid_when: No target is defined. A gauge without a goal is decoration; use a card.

intents.need: Compare a measure across named categories.
intents.question: Which business unit / product / site is highest?
intents.because: Microsoft: bar and column charts are better for comparing values because humans compare values side by side. Bars suit long category names.
intents.avoid_when: The category is time (use column or line).

intents.need: Compare a measure across a few discrete periods.
intents.question: How does this year compare with last year?
intents.because: Microsoft: use column charts for time-based comparisons. Columns read better than a line when there are only a handful of periods.
intents.avoid_when: More than about 12 periods: the shape of the trend matters more, so use a line.

intents.need: Show the shape of a measure over a continuous time axis.
intents.question: Is it rising, falling or seasonal?
intents.because: Line charts emphasise the overall shape of values over time.
intents.avoid_when: Fewer than about 4 points, or the category is not ordered time.

intents.need: Compare two measures whose magnitudes differ widely.
intents.question: How does volume relate to rate?
intents.because: Microsoft: avoid mixing large and small measures on the same scale; choose a visual that allows a second axis.
intents.avoid_when: Both measures share a scale and a unit: one column or line chart is clearer.

intents.need: Show how a few parts make up a total.
intents.question: What is the split?
intents.because: Microsoft: pie and donut charts are best with fewer than eight categories, and for part-to-whole relationships rather than for comparing parts.
intents.avoid_when: The point is to rank or compare the parts, or there are more than 6 slices: use a bar chart.

intents.need: Explain how a total moved from a start value to an end value.
intents.question: What drove the variance?
intents.because: Waterfall charts show a running total as values are added or subtracted.
intents.avoid_when: The measure is never negative: nothing subtracts, so a bar chart is honest and simpler.

intents.question: Where do we lose candidates / leads?
intents.because: Funnel charts visualise sequential processes where items flow from one stage to the next.
intents.avoid_when: The categories are not sequential stages, or values do not decrease.

intents.need: Let the reader look up precise numbers across several measures.
intents.question: What exactly did each cost center spend?
intents.because: Tables are ideal when you need exact values and quantitative comparison across many values.
intents.avoid_when: The reader only needs the ranking, not the numbers: a sorted bar chart is faster to read.

intents.need: Show where assets or values are located.
intents.question: Which sites, and where?
intents.because: Location is the message; a map makes spatial clustering visible.
intents.avoid_when: Position carries no meaning: use a bar chart.

intents.need: Test whether two measures move together.
intents.question: Does wind speed explain output?
intents.because: Scatter charts reveal correlations and clusters at the intersection of two numeric values.
intents.avoid_when: One axis is time: use a line.

intents.need: Let the reader narrow the page.
intents.question: Show me one entity / one year.
intents.avoid_when: More than about 3 slicers per page: move the rest to the filter pane.

intents.need: State the finding, the scope or the data caveat in words.
intents.question: What am I looking at, and what should I not conclude?
intents.because: Microsoft: text boxes add titles, descriptions and context; supplement colour with text so colour is never the only carrier of meaning.

intents.need: Identify the owning organisation or domain.
intents.question: Whose report is this?
intents.because: An image visual displays a company logo; keep it small, in one corner, and out of the tab order.
intents.avoid_when: It competes with the data for attention.

principles: Put the highest level of data top-left; add detail moving right and down, the way the audience reads.
Avoid variety for the sake of variety: a page with many different chart types is harder to read, not richer.
Do not exceed three or four numerals: scale to thousands or millions, because '3.4 million' reads faster than '3,400,000'.
Remove unnecessary data labels. If the eye is drawn more to labels than to data points, turn them off.
Be consistent with scales, category ordering and colours across the report.
Sort by the measure to expose extremes; sort by the axis when the reader needs to find a known category.
Never use colour as the only carrier of meaning: add text, icons or position.
Give every visual alt text; remove decorative images from the tab order.
Titles state the finding in the data, not the field names.
